title: Is Walmart gift card offer scam or real?
description: The company does offer a legitimate chance at a $1,000 gift card if you fill out a certain survey, but the ABC15 Investigators found the gift card text is a scam that has nothing to do with Walmart.

asr.full_text: One Thousand Dollar Walmart Gift Card. It's an offer you'll see in the Valley right now in two different forms. Tonight ABC 15 Investigator Joe Ducey discovered one offer is legitimate, and the other could cost you much more than a thousand bucks. You've just won a free $1,000 Walmart Gift Card enter M.A.R.T. to a certain number. It's a text scene around the valley. In five minutes, ten people told me about it on my ABC15 Facebook page. Christine says it's driving me insane. Angela gets so many it's extremely irritating, but it could be much worse if you answer. Walmart calls it a scam, saying people are asked to enter private information, credit card, or social security numbers on a website that could lead to theft or fraud. Walmartgift.mobi is the most common scam site according to Walmart we found it but couldn't open it doesn't matter another will take its place soon so don't answer any texts from a number you don't recognize now some good news Walmart does offer a chance for a legitimate thousand dollar gift card you have to fill out an online customer service survey you must enter a number from I HAVE SEEN DUTY THEN, THEY WERE GOING TO BE FOCUSING ON THESE THREATS. THAT COULD BE A CELL PHONE, A PAYMENT CARD, THINLY $1,000 GIFT CARDS, YOU HAVE TO FILL OUT AN ONLINE CUSTOMER SERVICE SURVEY. YOU MUST ENTER A NUMBER FROM YOUR WALMART RECEIPT BUT THERE IS NO PERSONAL INFORMATION REQUIRED. GO TO ABC15 DOT COM FOR CONSUMER ALERTS FOR MORE ON ALL OF THIS AND CHECK OUT ALL THE LATEST SCAMS THERE AND TELL ME ABOUT THEM. EMAIL ME OR GO TO MY ABC 15 FACEBOOK PAGE.

textual.observation: A message claims the viewer has won a free $1,000 Walmart gift card and directs them to enter a response to a number; the report also describes requests for private information, credit card numbers, or Social Security numbers on a website.

evidence.quote: You've just won a free $1,000 Walmart Gift Card enter M.A.R.T. to a certain number.
Walmart calls it a scam, saying people are asked to enter private information, credit card, or social security numbers on a website that could lead to theft or fraud.

textual.context: Presented in an investigative report with attribution to Walmart; the supplied record discusses the message as a reported scam and does not establish whether any particular recipient submitted information or experienced a loss.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised high-value gift card is linked to a text-response action and, according to the attributed report, to requests for sensitive personal and payment information, which warrants later assessment of the solicitation mechanism and destination.
textual.limitations: The records do not verify the sender, the phone number, the website's operation, whether the message was endorsed by Walmart, or any resulting transaction or harm.

textual.observation: The supplied description contrasts a legitimate company gift-card opportunity with gift-card text that investigators reported had nothing to do with Walmart.

evidence.quote: The company does offer a legitimate chance at a $1,000 gift card if you fill out a certain survey, but the ABC15 Investigators found the gift card text is a scam that has nothing to do with Walmart.

textual.context: The distinction is attributed to the description's reporting and is not independently verified by these records.
textual.potential_relevance: A $1,000 Walmart-associated reward is presented through two different channels, while the supplied source reports that the text-based version was unrelated to Walmart; the observable content-versus-association contrast may require later context assessment.
textual.limitations: No visual destination, sender identity, website content, or independent verification of the investigators' finding is provided.

textual.observation: The report describes a company gift-card opportunity tied to completing an online customer-service survey and entering a number from a Walmart receipt, while stating that personal information is not required.

evidence.quote: Walmart does offer a chance for a legitimate thousand dollar gift card you have to fill out an online customer service survey
YOU MUST ENTER A NUMBER FROM YOUR WALMART RECEIPT BUT THERE IS NO PERSONAL INFORMATION REQUIRED.

textual.context: Presented as a contrasting, reportedly legitimate offer in an investigative consumer-alert segment; the source's characterization is preserved rather than independently adopted.
textual.potential_relevance: A notable gift-card return is linked to a survey and a receipt-number condition, creating a concrete reward-and-action relationship for later assessment of the offer's terms and channel.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish the survey's operator, eligibility, fulfillment, or whether the stated conditions were accurately represented beyond this report.

visual.observation: A displayed text message claims the recipient has won a free $1,000 Walmart gift card and directs them to enter the word "1000" at a web address.
visual.context: The message is shown within a televised ABC15 Investigators segment titled "Free Walmart Gift Cards?"; the surrounding presentation is reporting/investigative context rather than an explicit audience promotion.
visual.potential_relevance: A high-value gift-card claim is directly linked to entering a term at an external destination, creating a concrete reward-and-action relationship for review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame does not establish who sent the message, what the destination does, whether the claim is valid, or whether anyone entered the term or received a card.

visual.observation: A displayed document instructs the recipient to visit a Walmart-branded survey web address and enter an identification code, stating that they could receive five $1,000 Walmart shopping cards in return.
visual.context: The document is presented as part of the same televised investigative report; the visible text also includes eligibility and survey-related conditions.
visual.potential_relevance: A substantial promised reward is linked to visiting a destination and submitting an identification code while using Walmart branding, which is a concrete reward, action, and claimed-affiliation relationship for review.
visual.limitations: The frame does not establish whether the document is authentic, what information the code identifies, whether payment or additional data was requested, or whether any reward was delivered.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as an ABC15 Investigators consumer report examining gift-card text messages rather than presenting those messages as its own offer. It warns that the reported messages may seek private, payment-card, or Social Security information and advises viewers not to answer texts from unrecognized numbers. The report separately describes a receipt-number customer-service survey opportunity and directs viewers to ABC15 consumer-alert material.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary context is an investigative warning that examines gift-card text messages, reports a claimed scam relationship, describes the information requests attributed to the message flow, and directs viewers to consumer-alert resources.
